title: ECDLP theorem, reduction, bound, attack, and open-obligation corpus

scope.statement: Classical and quantum ECDLP claims that determine what is proved, what is only model-relative, which curve families admit faster attacks, and which proof obligations remain live in this repository.
scope.completeness: The claim graph is a curated load-bearing backbone, not a flat exhaustive bibliography. The companion Galbraith inventory exhaustively indexes the numbered results and sections in that book, while this graph promotes the results that change an ECDLP, CDH, DDH, transfer, or protocol-security dependency.
scope.reduction_direction: For an edge A reduces_to B, an algorithm for B is sufficient to solve A. For hardness_implies, hardness of the source problem implies hardness of the destination problem.

sources.title: Lower Bounds for Discrete Logarithms and Related Problems
sources.citation: Victor Shoup, EUROCRYPT 1997, LNCS 1233, pp. 256-266.
sources.notes: Publisher PDF read. Theorem 1 gives success O(m^2/p) for generic DLP, with p the largest prime divisor of the group order.

sources.title: The Discrete-Logarithm Problem with Preprocessing
sources.citation: Henry Corrigan-Gibbs and Dmitry Kogan, EUROCRYPT 2018, LNCS 10820.
sources.notes: Publisher PDF read. Theorem 2 is the advice/online-time lower bound; Theorem 10 prices preprocessing time.

sources.title: An Improved Algorithm for Computing Logarithms over GF(p) and Its Cryptographic Significance
sources.citation: Stephen Pohlig and Martin Hellman, IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 24(1), 1978.
sources.notes: Author-hosted scan read. The algorithm decomposes the logarithm modulo prime-power factors and recombines by CRT.

sources.title: Monte Carlo Methods for Index Computation (mod p)
sources.citation: John M. Pollard, Mathematics of Computation 32(143), 1978, pp. 918-924.
sources.notes: Direct publisher PDF was inaccessible in this environment; the repository's portfolio and bibliography were read.

sources.title: The Discrete Logarithm Problem on Elliptic Curves of Trace One
sources.citation: Nigel P. Smart, Journal of Cryptology 12, 1999, pp. 193-196.
sources.notes: Publisher PDF read. The attack covers E/F_p with #E(F_p)=p and uses p-adic lifting.

sources.title: Reducing Elliptic Curve Logarithms to Logarithms in a Finite Field
sources.citation: Alfred Menezes, Tatsuaki Okamoto, and Scott Vanstone, IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 39(5), 1993.
sources.notes: Primary PDF was inaccessible. The reduction and its supersingular scope were cross-checked in Smart 1999 and repository sources.

sources.title: Constructive and Destructive Facets of Weil Descent on Elliptic Curves
sources.citation: Pierrick Gaudry, Florian Hess, and Nigel P. Smart, Journal of Cryptology 15, 2002, pp. 19-46.
sources.notes: Publisher PDF read. Theorem 1 is conditional on the transfer map's kernel not containing the large prime subgroup and fixes extension degree n.

sources.title: Summation Polynomials and the Discrete Logarithm Problem on Elliptic Curves
sources.citation: Igor Semaev, Cryptology ePrint Archive 2004/031.
sources.notes: The ePrint PDF returned HTTP 403. The defining property was checked in Diem 2011 and the repository's formal S3 work.

sources.title: On the Discrete Logarithm Problem in Elliptic Curves
sources.citation: Claus Diem, Compositio Mathematica 147(1), 2011, pp. 75-104.
sources.notes: Publisher PDF read. The main theorem gives expected time exp(O(max(log q,n^2))) for E/F_(q^n), with the paper's input conventions.

sources.title: Polynomial-Time Algorithms for Prime Factorization and Discrete Logarithms on a Quantum Computer
sources.citation: Peter W. Shor, SIAM Journal on Computing 26(5), 1997, pp. 1484-1509.
sources.notes: arXiv author version read. The paper gives polynomial-time quantum discrete-log algorithms for finite abelian groups.

sources.title: Do All Elliptic Curves of the Same Order Have the Same Difficulty of Discrete Log?
sources.citation: David Jao, Stephen D. Miller, and Ramarathnam Venkatesan, ASIACRYPT 2005.
sources.notes: Scope checked through the repository's theorem audit: random reducibility inside the same endomorphism ring under GRH, not across arbitrary volcano levels.

nodes.label: Elliptic-curve discrete logarithm problem
nodes.statement: Given a finite-field elliptic curve, a prime-order subgroup generated by P, and Q in the subgroup, recover x modulo r such that Q=[x]P.
nodes.scope: The curve model, field, subgroup order r, cofactor, generator, target distribution, and available auxiliary information are part of the instance.
assumptions: P has known prime order r

nodes.label: Named-curve classical ECDLP hardness assumption
nodes.statement: No feasible classical algorithm recovers a random scalar for the specified curve and subgroup within the declared resource bound.
nodes.scope: This is parameterized by a named curve/subgroup and a resource model; it is not a theorem implied by generic-group lower bounds.
assumptions: The instance excludes known weak families
The implementation does not leak the scalar
non_implications: Does not by itself imply CDH hardness
Does not by itself imply DDH hardness
Does not survive a scalable fault-tolerant quantum computer

nodes.label: Computational Diffie-Hellman
nodes.statement: Given P, [a]P, and [b]P in a cyclic subgroup, compute [ab]P.
nodes.scope: The distribution and subgroup are part of the problem definition.

nodes.label: Decisional Diffie-Hellman
nodes.statement: Given P, [a]P, [b]P, and R, decide whether R=[ab]P or is sampled from the comparison distribution.
nodes.scope: Pairings or other efficiently computable invariants can make DDH easy even when CDH and ECDLP remain apparently hard.

nodes.label: CDH reduces to ECDLP
nodes.statement: An ECDLP oracle recovers a and then computes [a]([b]P), so CDH is no harder than ECDLP.
nodes.scope: Black-box polynomial-time reduction in the same cyclic subgroup.
assumptions: The ECDLP oracle applies to the supplied subgroup

nodes.label: DDH reduces to CDH
nodes.statement: A CDH oracle computes [ab]P and compares it with R, so DDH is no harder than CDH.
nodes.scope: The comparison must use the same group and target distribution.

nodes.label: Prime-order DLP random self-reducibility
nodes.statement: An average-case DLP solver on a prime-order cyclic group can be blinded to obtain a solver for every instance with essentially the same success probability and only logarithmic overhead.
nodes.scope: Prime-order cyclic groups; the exact preprocessing variant fixes the group labeling and generator as in Corrigan-Gibbs--Kogan Lemma 3.

nodes.label: Pohlig-Hellman order decomposition
nodes.statement: DLP in a cyclic group of composite order reduces to DLPs in its prime-power order components and recombination by the Chinese remainder theorem.
nodes.scope: Security is controlled by the largest hard prime-order component, not by the total group order alone.
assumptions: The group order factorization is known or computed

nodes.label: Baby-step giant-step
nodes.statement: A generic meet-in-the-middle algorithm solves DLP in O(sqrt(r)) group operations and O(sqrt(r)) stored group elements.
nodes.scope: Prime-order subgroup of size r; constants and representations affect concrete cost.
assumptions: Equality testing and group operations are available

nodes.label: Pollard rho collision search
nodes.statement: Under the random-walk heuristic, rho solves prime-order DLP in expected O(sqrt(r)) group operations with negligible per-walker memory.
nodes.scope: The familiar sqrt(pi r/2) constant is an idealized collision model, not a universal implementation theorem.
assumptions: The iteration behaves sufficiently like a random mapping
Degenerate collisions and cycles are handled

nodes.label: Automorphism-folded rho
nodes.statement: Efficiently computable automorphisms with known scalar action can quotient the collision space and improve rho by an automorphism-dependent constant.
nodes.scope: The automorphism must preserve the subgroup and be accounted for on every compared method; fruitless cycles can erase the naive gain.
assumptions: Known scalar eigenvalue on the subgroup

nodes.label: Shoup generic DLP lower bound
nodes.statement: For a randomly encoded cyclic group whose order has largest prime divisor p, a generic algorithm making m oracle queries succeeds at DLP with probability O(m^2/p).
nodes.scope: Random encoding/generic oracle model. It does not cover algorithms exploiting coordinates, special representations, pairings, p-adic lifts, or algebraic equations.
assumptions: Only the declared generic group oracle and equality are exposed
nodes.formula: success = O(m^2/p); constant success => m = Omega(sqrt(p))

nodes.label: Shoup generic CDH lower bound
nodes.statement: The same generic-polynomial method yields an Omega(sqrt(p)) query lower bound for CDH at constant success when p is the relevant large prime divisor.
nodes.scope: Generic group model; not a statement that CDH and DLP are equivalent for concrete coordinate representations.

nodes.label: Generic preprocessing advice tradeoff
nodes.statement: For prime order N, a generic DLP algorithm with an S-bit group-specific advice string, at most T online oracle queries, and success epsilon satisfies S T^2 = soft-Omega(epsilon N).
nodes.scope: The paper's random-labeling generic model. S counts advice bits; preprocessing computation is ignored by this theorem and priced separately by another theorem.
assumptions: Group-specific advice independent of the target

nodes.label: Generic preprocessing-time tradeoff
nodes.statement: If generic group-specific preprocessing takes P operations, online time is T, and success is epsilon, then P T + T^2 = Omega(epsilon N).
nodes.scope: Same generic preprocessing model; this prices computation used to produce advice, not only stored advice length.

nodes.label: Smart anomalous-curve attack
nodes.statement: For E/F_p with #E(F_p)=p, p-adic lifting and the elliptic logarithm recover the discrete log in polynomial time; Smart describes linear time in the basic group-operation measure used there.
nodes.scope: Anomalous/trace-one prime-field curves only. A noncanonical lift succeeds except with probability 1/p and can be retried.

nodes.label: MOV pairing transfer
nodes.statement: When the subgroup embeds through a nondegenerate pairing into a low-degree finite-field multiplicative group, ECDLP reduces to finite-field DLP.
nodes.scope: Applicable when the embedding degree is small enough and the target-field DLP is easier; classically important for supersingular and other pairing-friendly cases.
assumptions: Subgroup order divides the target multiplicative group

nodes.label: GHS Weil-descent attack
nodes.statement: For the paper's characteristic-two composite-extension families and fixed n>=4, ECDLP in the large prime subgroup is solvable in O(q^(2+epsilon)) under the stated nonvanishing-kernel condition on the transfer map.
nodes.scope: Special extension fields and curves satisfying the paper's conditions. The constant has very bad n-dependence and the kernel hypothesis is explicit.
assumptions: The transfer map does not kill the large prime subgroup

nodes.label: Semaev summation-polynomial criterion
nodes.statement: The recursively defined summation polynomial vanishes exactly when compatible curve points with the supplied x-coordinates have signed sum equal to the identity, subject to the paper's field and multiplicity conventions.
nodes.scope: An algebraic encoding of a point-sum existence condition. It is not a complexity bound for solving the resulting polynomial system.
assumptions: The relevant x-coordinates lie in an algebraic closure
Exceptional and repeated-point cases use the stated conventions

nodes.label: Diem extension-field index calculus
nodes.statement: For E over F_(q^n), Diem gives a randomized algorithm with expected running time exp(O(max(log q,n^2))) in the paper's asymptotic input model.
nodes.scope: This yields subexponential families when n grows in the specified relation to log q. It is not a subexponential algorithm for fixed prime-field curves such as P-256 or secp256k1.
assumptions: The input is represented as in the theorem

nodes.label: Shor quantum discrete-log algorithm
nodes.statement: Discrete logarithms in finite abelian groups, including elliptic-curve subgroups, are solvable in time polynomial in the input length on a fault-tolerant quantum computer.
nodes.scope: Asymptotic quantum circuit model; concrete logical-qubit, gate, error-correction, and wall-time costs are separate engineering questions.

nodes.label: ECBND records are measured upper bounds
nodes.statement: An ecbench.bound/v1 record is the measured cost of one method configuration on a declared domain, with intervals and admissibility; it is not a lower bound on ECDLP.
nodes.scope: Toy, medium, and cryptographic tiers do not transfer automatically; each record is bound to its sessions, unit, curve family, and evidence.
assumptions: The record validates and its cited sessions/audits exist

nodes.label: Conditional generic simulation of table decomposition
nodes.statement: A decomposition computation whose setup and online phases use only generic group operations, public scalar actions, equality, and charged table lookup can be simulated in the generic interface.
nodes.scope: Conditional schema only. Representation-dependent indexing must be bookkeeping and must not reveal a coordinate predicate; no concrete pipeline is covered until its full interface is audited.
assumptions: All advice is built generically or its extra information is modeled
Every online predicate is generically simulable
Advice and lookup costs are charged

nodes.label: Mean decomposition-yield conservation
nodes.statement: A double-counting argument fixes the mean ordered decomposition multiplicity over the full target domain for a fixed factor-base size and arity.
nodes.scope: Controls mean multiplicity, not variance, rank, search cost, specialization behavior, or the cost of recognizing a decomposition.
assumptions: The sum map and target averaging domain are exactly the ones in the theorem
Ordered tuples use the stated convention

nodes.label: Isogeny-augmented generic lower bound
nodes.statement: With independent random encodings for prime-order subgroups and public scalar action for each isogeny, isogeny-oracle queries preserve linear formal expressions and retain birthday-order DLP hardness.
nodes.scope: Generic subgroup interface only. Coordinate access, map construction cost, pairings, p-adic lifts, and arbitrary coordinate-generated points are outside the theorem.
assumptions: Known scalar action of each map

nodes.label: JMV random reduction within an isogeny stratum
nodes.statement: Under GRH, random reducibility relates ECDLP instances on curves with the same endomorphism ring through an expander walk.
nodes.scope: Does not give a free reduction across arbitrary conductor gaps or a concrete same-cost solver across all curves of the same order.
assumptions: The reduction's walk and map costs are charged

nodes.label: Frobenius-stable subspaces at n=131
nodes.statement: For the degree-131 binary extension used by ECC2K-130, Frobenius-stable F_2-subspaces have dimensions 0, 1, 130, or 131.
nodes.scope: Uses the factorization of X^131-1 over F_2 and ord_131(2)=130; it obstructs intermediate-size invariant linear factor bases, not arbitrary nonlinear bases.
assumptions: The subspace is F_2-linear and Frobenius-stable

nodes.label: GHS genus classification at n=131
nodes.statement: The repository's GHS analysis for the ECC2K-130 degree-131 setting yields only genus 1, 2^130-1, or 2^130 in the classified construction.
nodes.scope: Obstructs that GHS construction for the exact prime extension degree; it is not a theorem that every possible cover or Jacobian transfer has huge genus.

nodes.label: Current measured classical frontier
nodes.statement: The repository records scoped, validated costs for generic algorithms and index-calculus variants; these identify the best measured method on shared toy/medium domains and expose missing coverage.
nodes.scope: The frontier is per exact domain and evidence class. It cannot establish asymptotic hardness or transfer a toy result to a cryptographic curve.
assumptions: Each entry is compared only on shared sizes and axes
Admissibility and validation state are respected

nodes.label: No unconditional classical ECDLP lower bound
nodes.statement: No known theorem proves a superpolynomial classical lower bound for ECDLP on a named standard elliptic curve in the unrestricted computation model.
nodes.scope: This is a statement about the present proof boundary, not evidence that a faster algorithm exists.

nodes.label: Coordinate-algebraic escape from generic bounds
nodes.statement: Shoup and Corrigan-Gibbs--Kogan do not rule out an algorithm that uses curve coordinates, low-degree membership predicates, polynomial systems, pairings, or other representation-specific structure.
nodes.scope: Every proposed escape must still price relation yield, system construction, solving, lifting, linear algebra, target descent, and verification.

nodes.label: Preprocessing bounds with automorphism quotients
nodes.statement: Applying the preprocessing tradeoff after quotienting by efficiently computable automorphisms needs an explicit oracle model and orbit accounting; replacing N by an effective orbit count is not automatic.
nodes.scope: Covers the proof bridge between known scalar actions, quotient encodings, advice size, and online queries.

nodes.label: Prime-field PKM solving-degree growth
nodes.statement: It is unresolved whether the solving degree of the PKM tower systems remains bounded or resumes growth beyond the measured N<=18/20 frontier.
nodes.scope: A bounded degree would only establish a live asymptotic route after solution counts, constants, and complete pipeline costs are also controlled.

nodes.label: Binary m=4 Weil-descent degree growth
nodes.statement: The m=4 degree behavior for prime-degree binary fields is measured only at small dimensions and does not determine the degree at n=83 or n=131.
nodes.scope: The gap includes both a mathematical growth law and conversion from solver work to the same unit as the reference algorithm.

nodes.label: Coordinate transport-oracle simulation
nodes.statement: An exact same-cost simulation theorem for coordinate-aware transport oracles on arbitrary factor-base points has not been proved; the earlier internal claim was withdrawn.
nodes.scope: Requires explicit algebraic representations, quantifier order, allowed point generation, map evaluation cost, and a same-input reduction.

nodes.label: Concrete fault-tolerant quantum resources
nodes.statement: Shor settles asymptotic quantum tractability, while concrete resources for a named curve depend on reversible arithmetic, error correction, architecture, and failure probability.
nodes.scope: An engineering/resource-estimation question, not a remaining asymptotic hardness assumption against quantum algorithms.

nodes.label: Specific-curve hardness remains assumption-based
nodes.statement: After order checks and known special-family attacks are excluded, generic lower bounds and the absence of a known faster coordinate attack support parameter selection but do not prove unrestricted classical hardness for the named curve.
nodes.scope: The conclusion must be restated for each curve, subgroup, auxiliary-information model, preprocessing allowance, and adversary class.

Square-root lower bound for generic CDH at constant success.
Advice/online-time lower bound in the generic preprocessing model.
Preprocessing-work/online-time lower bound in the same model.

Applies to the classified characteristic-two extension families and a non-killed subgroup image.

Gives an unrestricted-in-instance expected-time upper bound for the paper's extension-field parameterization.

Birthday-order lower bound in the isogeny-augmented generic subgroup model.
Supports random reducibility only within its GRH and endomorphism-ring scope.

Binary Weil-descent degree growth is a concrete algebraic-coordinate question outside generic lower bounds.
Concrete resources remain open even though asymptotic quantum tractability is settled.
The absence of an unrestricted lower bound is why named-curve classical security remains assumption-based.
Provides rigorous evidence only for generic algorithms.
Provides rigorous evidence against generic preprocessing attacks in its advice model.
A named curve must exclude the anomalous-order condition.
A named curve must have an adequately large embedding degree after target-field DLP pricing.
Security must be stated for the large prime subgroup, not the full curve order alone.
The classical qualifier is essential because the asymptotic quantum problem is polynomial-time.

research_targets.label: Concrete generic-interface audit
research_targets.objective: For every method currently classified as generic decomposition, enumerate setup and online operations and prove or refute that each coordinate key/predicate is generically simulable under the Shoup/CGK interfaces.
research_targets.acceptance: A method-by-method matrix names every non-group operation, advice dependency, lookup semantics, and charged counter; each method is covered by a proved simulation statement or is reclassified with the exact escaping predicate.
research_targets.next_step: Trace the live generic-decomposition methods from classification.json into the ecbench registry and group implementation, starting with prime subtract, prime MITM/pair-table, and Koblitz compact-orbit methods.

research_targets.label: Algebraic factor-base solution-count falsifier
research_targets.objective: Compute or prove the algebraic-closure solution count for membership-constrained Semaev systems and compare it with B^(m-1).
research_targets.acceptance: Exact counts or certified degrees for PKM, Dickson, subgroup, and random-control bases across the frozen small ladder, with the count convention and multiplicity stated.
research_targets.next_step: Port the existing proposed census to a native producer and freeze the m=2,3 toy ladder before execution.

research_targets.label: PKM solving-degree growth
research_targets.objective: Determine whether the observed solving-degree plateau survives at N=21,24,27 and reconcile it with Hilbert-series predictions.
research_targets.acceptance: At least three independent systems per rung, actual solver degree, peak memory, retained failures, and a checked Hilbert-series predictor that agrees on prior rungs.
research_targets.next_step: Materialize the current native system exporter and design an EKS-compatible high-memory run; do not infer bounded degree from the existing plateau.

research_targets.label: Prime-degree binary m=4 degree ladder
research_targets.objective: Extend exact m=4 Weil-descent degree measurements and calibrate solver work into the same unit as the matched generic reference.
research_targets.acceptance: Matched representations, three or more larger degree cells, exact closure/solver degree, memory, and an independently checked work-unit conversion.
research_targets.next_step: Audit the current G2 equivariant-F4 and m=4 system exporters before freezing cells; the lead atlas changed since review, so collision-check the latest records first.

research_targets.label: Coordinate transport-oracle theorem
research_targets.objective: Prove a same-input, same-cost simulation theorem for the largest defensible coordinate-aware transport interface, or construct a concrete counterexample interface.
research_targets.acceptance: Explicit quantifier order, allowed algebraic representations, point-generation rules, map costs, and a proof or counterexample checked against the withdrawn claim.
research_targets.next_step: Start from the R6.8 counterexample boundary and separate transport of received points from transport of newly coordinate-generated factor-base points.

research_targets.label: Automorphism-aware preprocessing model
research_targets.objective: State and prove the preprocessing tradeoff for a generic group augmented with a finite known-scalar automorphism action, including advice units and orbit stabilizers.
research_targets.acceptance: A theorem with explicit oracle semantics and success probability, or a reduction to the original CGK model that accounts for the encoding of orbit representatives.
research_targets.next_step: Write the finite-action oracle and attempt a reduction with N replaced only after proving the orbit/stabilizer distribution.

research_targets.label: Named-curve fault-tolerant resource ladder
research_targets.objective: Reduce concrete reversible point-addition, inversion, and error-correction resources for named curves without confusing resource improvements with restored asymptotic hardness.
research_targets.acceptance: Verified reversible circuits, full-input correctness, logical resource accounting, and architecture/error-rate assumptions for each estimate.
research_targets.next_step: Continue the lead-atlas safegcd/jump-GCD inversion target on the existing secp256k1 circuit baseline.
